purpose: Pre-register deterministic human-quality sampling before any M6 optimizer outputs exist, preventing result-aware cherry-picking while ensuring high-risk strata receive review.
scope: sampling infrastructure only; selects review workload and never decides a deck change

authority.note: Selection into a review stratum creates an obligation to inspect; it is not negative evidence and never approves or rejects a deck.

selection.dedupe_for_total_workload: yes_after_per_stratum_selection; every selected stratum membership remains visible
selection.quota_shortfall: select all eligible candidates; never pad from ineligible decks
selection.policy_mutation_after_freeze: forbidden without Cory explicit approval; any change requires a superseding version and keeps this v1 file/hash in history

strata.rationale: Unbiased coverage catches defects not anticipated by targeted risk strata.

strata.ranking_rule: anomaly count descending, then deterministic tie break
strata.rationale: Cards whose structural and popularity/evidence signals disagree are likely places for ranking/model mistakes.

strata.candidate_rule: registry deck has project_exceptions or project_authorization_status is not none
strata.rationale: Project authorization must remain separate from official legality and is too consequential to sample away.

strata.candidate_rule: registry state is PENDING_RELEASE or official_commander_compliance.status is pending_release
strata.rationale: Future-release legality and snapshot transitions require explicit human attention.

strata.candidate_rule: resolved ceiling is 5 when present, otherwise grok_estimated_ceiling/source_ceiling is 5
strata.rationale: B5 decks have tighter timing, stack and compact-win tolerances than B4 decks.

strata.ranking_rule: accepted role rank supporting < significant < central; then commander-linked combo fraction ascending; then explicit-commander Blueprint win fraction ascending; then deterministic tie break
strata.rationale: These are the decks most at risk of drifting into generically powerful Grixis shells despite Commander-first goals.

strata.candidate_rule: all decks with M1 interaction review
strata.ranking_rule: rules-risk score descending: 3 * non-verified interaction count + key interaction count + Blueprint construction-rule count + 2 if project-exception/pending-release; then deterministic tie break
strata.rationale: Dense or unresolved rules dependencies are high-risk for superficially plausible but invalid refinements.

strata.candidate_rule: both independently blinded optimizer outputs are committed and hashed for the deck
strata.ranking_rule: challenger-list hash disagreement first; then swap-pair symmetric-difference count descending; then count of cards cut by one pass and retained by the other descending; then deterministic tie break
strata.rationale: Human review must concentrate where the two independent objective functions disagree most; the formula is frozen before results exist.

strata.candidate_rule: reconciled challenger has at least 5 swaps OR changes a declared win route/package OR changes at least 3 mana-base slots
strata.ranking_rule: win-route change first; then required-package change count descending; then total swaps descending; then mana-base changes descending; then deterministic tie break
strata.rationale: Large structural changes deserve mandatory review even when optimizer agreement is high; the trigger and ranking are frozen before M6 results exist.

high_optimizer_disagreement.swap_identity: ordered cut=>add pair string; pair order within each pass ignored for set comparison

major_change.note: Selection occurs before APPROVAL_READY and before Cory sees a recommendation packet; no post-hoc reviewer choice changes the formula.

limitations: Sampling improves human oversight coverage; it does not prove unsampled decks are correct.
Strata may overlap substantially and that overlap is intentional.
Static risk metrics are review-priority diagnostics, not deck-quality scores.
Future dynamic strata cannot be populated until their pre-registered M6-stage inputs exist.
Cory may review more decks than the sampler selects; the sampler is a minimum review obligation, not a maximum.
